boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Atlanta record (July 22, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. The capture of the bald hill on July 21 and the siege that followed are context; Wheeler's attack at Decatur the same day is part of Cox's account. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the two armies without counts; the live field reads zero. Cox calls the first attack one of four divisions upon four, names Hardee's divisions (Maney, Cleburne, Walker, Bate), and gives Hood's July 31 return (present 65,601, effectives 44,495) in Appendix A. Hood says Hardee moved with his corps and Wheeler's cavalry on his right, with Cheatham to take up the attack; his army's effective strength on July 18 was 48,750.
claims.rationale: Division counts and army totals at different dates (July 18 and July 31) and bases; none measures the troops engaged and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Hood says Hardee failed to turn the enemy's left as directed. Cox rejects Hood's complaint about Hardee's march; says a refused request to burn the house helped cause the break in the Fifteenth Corps line; that Sherman ordered Schofield's artillery onto the break; and that Sherman put Logan in command after McPherson's death. The frozen commanders are General John Bell Hood and Major General William T. Sherman; the live page gives General William Sherman and General John Hood.
claims.rationale: Attributed judgments in dispute from interested accounts; Hardee, McPherson and Logan are not listed commanders; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live ranks are not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Hood says Hardee held the ground he gained, Cheatham carried works but had to abandon them, McPherson's movement on his communications was entirely defeated though the grand results were not achieved, and the engagement revived the troops' confidence. Cox says the Fifteenth Corps counter-charge retook the line and all but two lost guns, and the crisis passed. NPS says the Union troops held.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Hood's campaign-level claim about McPherson's movement is not the tactical result.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 12,140 (US 3,641; CS 8,499). Cox gives the Union loss as 3,521 with ten guns; counts about 3,200 Confederate dead delivered or buried (partly estimated), halves the estimated part to reach at least 2,500 killed, adds 2,000 prisoners and accepts Logan's ten thousand as the minimum. Hood says Cheatham took 5 guns and Hardee 8 guns and 13 colours.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Cox's Confederate total is an inference from burial counts; the frozen Union 3,641 differs from Cox's 3,521.

open_questions: Logan's July 24 summary and July 22 report (casualty lines seen by search, not selected), Blair's, Dodge's and Schofield's reports, Hardee's and Cheatham's accounts, Govan's and Smith's brigade reports and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Hood's February 15, 1865 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, is a third family (interested Confederate account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
